findings.title: Duplicate MRNs across different patient keys
findings.evidence: patients GROUP BY mrn HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
findings.interpretation: MRN cannot be used as a unique cross-system identity key.

findings.title: CRM/clinical dob disagreements
findings.evidence: data/raw/crm_patient_export.csv joined to clinical_patient_export.csv on patient_key; compare dob
findings.interpretation: Identity evidence differs across source-specific views and requires explainable reconciliation.

findings.title: CRM/clinical center_id disagreements
findings.evidence: data/raw/crm_patient_export.csv joined to clinical_patient_export.csv on patient_key; compare center_id
findings.interpretation: Identity evidence differs across source-specific views and requires explainable reconciliation.

findings.title: CRM/clinical mrn disagreements
findings.evidence: data/raw/crm_patient_export.csv joined to clinical_patient_export.csv on patient_key; compare mrn
findings.interpretation: Identity evidence differs across source-specific views and requires explainable reconciliation.

findings.title: CRM/clinical name_or_alias disagreements
findings.evidence: data/raw/crm_patient_export.csv joined to clinical_patient_export.csv on patient_key; compare name_or_alias
findings.interpretation: Identity evidence differs across source-specific views and requires explainable reconciliation.

findings.title: MES released while QMS not released
findings.interpretation: Manufacturing/MES state must not substitute for Quality release authority.

findings.title: ERP available while QMS not released
findings.interpretation: Commercial/inventory availability can conceal an unmet Quality gate.

findings.title: Journeys classified ready by unsafe legacy heuristic
findings.evidence: Legacy product_ready predicate reproduced against batches and joined gate evidence
findings.interpretation: A positive legacy readiness result does not prove patient/product readiness; multiple safety dependencies are omitted.
findings.caveat: Categories overlap and must not be summed.

findings.title: Stored journey status ahead of Quality release
findings.evidence: patients joined to batches; journey_status vs qms_release_status
findings.interpretation: Stored journey strings cannot be trusted as authoritative gate decisions.

findings.title: Consent states requiring explicit gating
findings.interpretation: Withdrawn and expired-version consent cannot be ignored by downstream readiness.

findings.title: Authorization states requiring explicit gating
findings.interpretation: Authorization status affects scheduling and downstream commercial/process readiness.

findings.title: Open/investigating deviations and Quality-release coexistence
findings.interpretation: Open deviations require blocking classification and disposition evidence; open status alone does not prove every release invalid.

findings.title: Deviation links do not resolve to the event log
findings.interpretation: Quality investigations lack resolvable event evidence.

findings.title: QMS-released batches with pending/OOS/OOT QC rows
findings.evidence: batches joined to qc_results; qms release with result in PENDING/OOS/OOT
findings.interpretation: Explicit assay disposition evidence is required before interpreting these rows.

findings.title: Treatment centers with expired training or due equipment
findings.interpretation: High-level site status can obscure detailed qualification controls.

findings.title: Shipments arriving before departure
findings.interpretation: Physical event ordering contradicts recorded shipment timestamps.

findings.title: Patient histories whose recorded order inverts occurrence order
findings.evidence: events grouped by patient and sorted by recorded_at; adjacent occurred_at inversion
findings.interpretation: Recorded order and physical occurrence order are separate concepts.

findings.title: Maximum event recording lag in hours
findings.interpretation: Late-arriving evidence can change a derived journey view.

findings.title: Retry-duplicate manufacturing-start events
findings.interpretation: New event identifiers do not guarantee semantic uniqueness or idempotency.

findings.title: Scheduler-confirmed slots cancelled in MES
findings.interpretation: Partial distributed state and absent compensation create unreliable capacity state.

findings.title: Formal vs shadow patient-priority disagreements
findings.evidence: manufacturing_slots.csv joined to PatientPriority_MASTER.csv on patient_key
findings.interpretation: Operational priority is being maintained outside the formal scheduling view.

findings.title: Manufacturing-slot rows containing planner override notes
findings.interpretation: Email/manual decisions create downstream dependencies not represented as governed transactions.

findings.title: Shadow email categories
findings.interpretation: Unstructured email carries slot, courier, identity, Quality and site-readiness coordination.

findings.title: Courier escalations requiring closed-loop ownership
findings.interpretation: Open or unowned escalation work can delay patient/material movement without accountable resolution.

findings.title: Telemetry and excursion evidence requiring contextual disposition
findings.interpretation: A point threshold is insufficient; effective SOP v7 requires duration, quality, cumulative profile, shipper integrity and human Quality review.

findings.title: Booked/in-transit shipments with arrival timestamps
findings.evidence: shipments status IN (BOOKED,IN_TRANSIT) with arrived_at populated
findings.interpretation: Shipment state and event evidence disagree; neither should be silently preferred.

findings.title: Event model covers only a narrow set of business events
findings.interpretation: Consent, authorization, site qualification, slot, QC, deviation, QA release, conditioning and infusion are not first-class events.
